title: Understanding SVD Dimensions
text: In Singular Value Decomposition (SVD), the matrix $X$ is decomposed into three matrices: $U$, $S$, and $V**T$. Each of these matrices has specific dimensions based on the dimensions of $X$.

title: Dimensions of $U$
text: The matrix $U$ in the SVD of $X$ has dimensions $n \times n$. This is because $U$ is an orthogonal matrix that spans the column space of $X$.

title: Dimensions of $V$
text: The matrix $V$ in the SVD of $X$ has dimensions $d \times d$. This is because $V$ is an orthogonal matrix that spans the row space of $X$.

title: Dimensions of $S$
text: The matrix $S$ in the SVD of $X$ is a diagonal matrix with dimensions $n \times d$. It contains the singular values of $X$.

title: Checking the Observation
text: Given the dimensions of $U$, $S$, and $V$, check if the statement "The dimensions of $U$ and $V$ must be the same" is true or false.
